TICKET 1c4ae8f053fe IS PROVED AND PUSHED (cairn f49c5dd, CairnCommons 486256f, both clean, verified by orient.git not by narration). The seal now snapshots the instance root ONCE per batch and skips the trail tree: 888.7MB/9.28s/163,352 entries per sealed proof down to 118.0MB/0.34s/3,620 for a batch's first proof and 0.09s for each after. Both sides came from one instrument — HEAD's own snapshot code loaded as a live module — so the before figure is measured, not remembered.

THE VOYAGE ALSO FIXED A BUG IT UNCOVERED, under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage (Akien: 'we are just going to attach that to the same ticket as a bug we fix with it'; confirmed 'agreed on all counts. ruled approved and boogied'). The emptier sandbox exposed a HOLLOW GREEN: inference_domain's probe resolved its trail through two doors and only the first followed the device, so for two months its tooth passed on the LIVE trail's borrowed lines rather than on the one line it wrote — its bound was `>= 1`, which both trails meet. Fixed at the BASE CLASS where the shape cannot come back: DiagnosticBase gained diagnostic_records() beside diagnostic_trail(), so WHERE and WHAT are one answer both carrying the device's roots. Measured both ways: fixed reads trail_misses=1, reverted reads 3312. Four new teeth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_device_logs_unwired.py (38 assertions, green twice) and both mutations bite. `ruling verify` reads green.

93 VALIDATIONS RE-SEALED across 25 components — blast radius measured by scanning evidence.fingerprint_closure, not guessed. The berthed chart packets were NOT edited: rewriting constrain's bounds.in backward would make the record lie about what the chart knew on the day it was charted, so the widening is recorded forward only.

Standing mandate in force: sail every ticket in a tier back to back, return only at tier completion or when something needs a ruling. TIER 1 REMAINS: d0f2b03952e3, 4d9115eb04cd, 8754ae677af6, feeb4c786b14 (PROVEME:waiting), 1accdc1781aa (BUILDME:queued). Then tiers 2-4 of the 35-ticket queue.
next_direction: Next ticket in tier 1 (d0f2b03952e3), then the rest of the tier back to back, reporting at the tier boundary. Before or during that, cast the tickets this voyage owes — they are findings, and a finding that lives only in a slate teaches nobody.

TICKETS OWED, NOT YET CAST (this voyage added the first two):
1. A WEAKER SEAL MAY SILENTLY OVERWRITE A STRONGER ONE. Measured today: re-sealing bare (`--seal` without `--netns`) replaced `seal:{verdict:sealed}` with `seal:{verdict:open, detail:'none: no seal requested'}` across 44 validations, and nothing refused it. Caught only by diffing test_diagnostic.json by hand.
2. THE TESTER'S OWN PROOFS CANNOT NEST UNDER AN INSTANCE SEAL. Measured: test_isolation and test_instance_seal are green bare and RED under --netns (no baseline route to 1.1.1.1 inside a netns means the seal cannot prove it removed anything — honestly indeterminate; and a nested subject's write reaches the OUTER sandbox's 'live' root). build_inspector/test_inspector times out at 120s inside one. All three carry `seal: open` + `instance_seal: sealed` at HEAD and were restored to exactly that.
